title: Constraint-aware and Ranking-distilled Token Pruning for Efficient Transformer Inference

problem.claim: Deploying pretrained transformer models such as BERT in resource-constrained scenarios is difficult because inference cost increases rapidly with input sequence length.

gap.claim: Conventional self-attention produces inaccurate token-importance rankings for pruning decisions in early layers.

contributions.claim: ToP selectively removes unnecessary tokens as inputs pass through transformer layers to improve online inference speed while preserving accuracy.
ToP distills effective token rankings from the final layer of unpruned models to early layers of pruned models.
ToP uses coarse-to-fine pruning to select transformer layers and optimize token-pruning decisions with improved L0 regularization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ToP outperforms state-of-the-art token-pruning and model-compression methods on GLUE and SQuAD with improved accuracy and speedups.
The authors report an average 8.1X reduction in BERT FLOPs with competitive GLUE accuracy.
The authors report real latency speedups of up to 7.4X on an Intel CPU.

narrative_sequence.summary: Resource-constrained deployment of BERT is challenged by inference costs that grow with sequence length.
ToP prunes unnecessary tokens during layer-wise inference while targeting speed improvements and accuracy preservation.
Ranking distillation transfers effective token rankings from final unpruned layers to early pruned layers.
A coarse-to-fine strategy selects pruning layers and optimizes decisions through improved L0 regularization.
Experiments on GLUE and SQuAD report improved accuracy and speed, including reductions in FLOPs and CPU latency.
